title: The right to be forgotten - its constitutional basis being tested in courts
p1:
Can something you posted years ago continue to define you forever?

The internet remembers everything, but should the law allow people to move on?
p2:
Many believe the right to be forgotten means deleting any unwanted information from the internet. That is not the complete picture. It is about balancing a person's privacy and dignity with the public's right to access information.

A surprising fact: this right is not explicitly written as a separate fundamental right in the Indian Constitution. Courts have been examining whether it can be protected through the broader right to privacy under Article 21.
p3:
The real challenge is deciding where to draw the line. A person may want old personal details removed, but society may still have a valid reason to access certain information.

Courts are now testing how privacy, reputation, freedom of expression, and public interest can coexist in the digital age.

The takeaway: your digital past matters, but the law is exploring whether everyone deserves a chance to rewrite their digital future.
conclusion: Should people have a legal right to remove old online information about themselves, or could that affect society's right to know?
